pr.title: Plan putting a branch's iOS app on a device with project ios
pr.head: 7bb13044661b5bf0206fdb0c4a4472802d16f996

summary: Projector's inbox lets an agent ask the person to test a change on their phone. The agent posts a request whose start action is the one thing the agent does when the person presses start, such as installing a build. Projector supplies the request but nothing to build or install with, so each iOS repository writes its own script.

This pull request adds a plan, docs/projects/ios/readme.md, at status: ready and priority: now. It proposes a project ios command group that ports one repository's 500-line device-test shell script to a standard-library Python module. Nothing is implemented yet. The plan is the whole change, and a later two-layer stack will carry the code and the skill text.

• build <branch-or-number> fetches a branch or a pull request's head into one worktree that Projector keeps per repository. It builds the head with xcodebuild into one shared DerivedData folder, keeps a copy of the built app for that target, and installs and opens it on the one connected device. It refuses an untrusted pull request head unless the person passes --allow-untrusted.
  • install puts a kept build on a device again, so a start action installs the target it names rather than whatever was built last.
  • devices, crashes, logs, and cleanup list paired devices, copy and summarize crash reports, write the app's recent log lines to a file, and remove the worktree and the builds.

The app is found by convention: the scheme is <App> Development, or else <App>, where <App> defaults to the Xcode project's name. Three new settings, ios.app, ios.project, and ios.output, cover repositories that do not follow it.

cards.title: Where the review stands
cards.html:
The review of 7bb1304 is clean. The first review, of 1857f02, raised three findings, and the author fixed each one:

  • Untrusted heads. build now judges a pull request's head with review.trusted_head and refuses an untrusted one unless the person passes --allow-untrusted. That flag has its own ask rule.
  • Log filter. § 2.4's subsystem rule now leaves out a two-part vendor prefix such as com.example, as § 4 requires.
  • Linux CI. § 4 now gives stand-ins for log, sudo, open, and cp, and step 8 uses shutil.copytree off macOS.

The author took five of the six suggestions. build still installs by default.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• Start action: what the agent does when the person presses start on a request. The press is the person's consent.
  • Kept build: a copy of the built app under builds/<App>/<key>/, with a build.json that records its commit and bundle ID. The key is pr-<number> or branch- plus the percent-encoded branch name.
  • Trusted head: a head in this repository whose pull request author and commit authors all have write access, by the rule project review setup uses.
  • DerivedData: Xcode's build folder. Because one is shared, a branch switch rebuilds only what changed.
  • devicectl: Apple's command-line tool, run through xcrun, that lists paired devices, installs apps on them, and launches those apps.

groups.title: The project ios plan
groups.kicker: A ready plan for building, installing, and debugging an iOS app from any branch
intro: The plan's ready status claims that every question that blocks implementation is answered. Read it with that claim in mind. § 1 is the problem, § 2.1 the commands and options, § 2.2 the build flow, § 2.3 how the app is found, and § 2.4 crashes and logs. § 2.5 covers the state on disk, § 2.6 the skill changes, and § 2.7 the files the change touches. The plan gives its reasons in § 3 and its acceptance tests in § 4.

The plan's claims about the code it builds on hold at this head. review.fetch writes no FETCH_HEAD. review.fetch_head already chooses between a pull request's branch and refs/pull/<n>/head, and review.trusted_head already holds the trust rule. config.SETTINGS holds only flat, typed keys. The implement skill already keeps a pull request a draft during a device test.

checks.text: At this head, project check passes and git diff --check against the merge base is clean. The unit suite passed at 1857f02, and the change since then touches only the plan.

files.note: The new plan for project ios: commands, build flow, app convention, state, skill changes, permissions, and acceptance tests.

checks.text: The trust rule § 2.2 step 4 describes matches review.trusted_head, and exit 65 is ProjectorError's status. ASK, ASKED, CODEX_ALLOW, and CODEX_RULES are the names permissions.py uses.

build still installs by default. An agent that runs project ios build <n> without --no-install replaces the build on the person's device. § 2.6 tells agents to pass --no-install and install only on STARTED.
